newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan govt unveils economic structural reform plan.
newsitem.headline: Japan govt unveils economic structural reform plan.

text.p: Japan unveiled its programme for the structural reform of the economy on Thursday.

It recommends deregulatory measures and the promotion of new businesses in 15 areas considered to have potential for growth and aims to bring down costs in those areas to international levels by 2001.
In particular, it targets the energy sector, aiming to stir up competition within the heavily regulated power utilities industry. Telecommunications and human resources are other key areas.
The report, compiled by the Ministry of International Trade, follows an initial policy plan outlined last December.
It is part of Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's efforts to reform the economy, including "Big Bang" financial reforms. The government will formally adopt the programme in a cabinet meeting on Friday
Following are the main points of the programme.
Energy:
-- Improve capacity utilisation rates in order to cut costs
-- Increase efficiency in the the purchase of parts and equipment and step up efforts to streamline management
-- Create more competition in the electricity sector
-- Promote independent power producers and provide an environment in which they can compete fairly within a year
-- Cut electricity rates in 1998 and urge the industry to cut rates further in 2000
FINANCE
-- Invigorate the financial markets and promote ways of channelling capital to venture businesses
-- Lift the ban on broking of unlisted or unregistered stocks by securities companies by the end of June
-- Complete "Big Bang" financial reforms by 2001.
TELECOMMUNICATIONS
-- Review the rate approval system and implement rate setting regulations that will allow for easier rate cuts by the end of fiscal 1999/2000.
-- Look to lower connection costs and examine new methods of calculating access charges.
-- Build a digital network infrastructure system, connecting digitised, wireless, mobile and fixed communications systems.
-- Review laws relating to electronic money and other systems so that electronic commerce will be in use by companies and consumers by 2001.
FOREIGN CAPITAL
-- Cut regulations over foreign investment, except for security-related laws, by 2001.
DISTRIBUTION
-- Review the large-scale retail Law, to be completed by December
PENSIONS
-- Review private firms' pension systems.
